edits.text: 1. Purchase Price. The Seller proposes a purchase price of USD 45,000,000 for the Shares. The treatment of cash, debt and normalized working capital, including the applicable definitions, target, calculation methodology and adjustment procedures, remains subject to agreement in definitive documentation. The proposed transaction remains subject to satisfactory diligence, required approvals and agreement on definitive terms.

2. Closing. Closing shall occur on a date agreed by the parties following satisfaction or, where legally permissible, waiver by the party entitled to the benefit of the applicable conditions set out in the definitive agreement. Those conditions shall include required regulatory and corporate approvals and other mutually agreed customary closing conditions. The definitive agreement shall specify an agreed long-stop date and associated termination rights.

3. Representations, Disclosure and Indemnification. The definitive agreement shall contain mutually agreed customary Seller representations concerning title to the Shares, authority, accounts, undisclosed liabilities, tax, material contracts, litigation and compliance with applicable law. Their scope shall be subject to negotiated materiality and knowledge qualifications and appropriate disclosures in an agreed disclosure letter and schedules. The parties shall agree the process and standard for disclosure, including the treatment of due-diligence materials. Any indemnification provisions shall be negotiated together with applicable caps, baskets, time limits, claim procedures, mitigation obligations and protections against double recovery. Supporting financial information and proposed disclosure materials shall be made available through an agreed diligence process, subject to applicable law, privilege and appropriate confidentiality protections.

4. Confidentiality. The existence and terms of the proposed transaction and non-public information exchanged in connection with it shall be kept confidential and used only to evaluate, finance or implement the transaction. A party may disclose such information to its advisers and actual or prospective financing sources who need to know it for those purposes and are bound by confidentiality obligations or professional duties of confidentiality. Disclosure may also be made to the extent required by law, regulation or a competent authority, provided that, where legally permitted, the disclosing party gives advance notice and reasonably cooperates in seeking confidential treatment. Confidentiality restrictions shall not apply to information lawfully in the public domain other than through a breach of confidentiality. Any existing confidentiality agreement remains unaffected unless expressly amended in writing.

receiver.requested_changes: Replace the Seller's USD 45,000,000 proposal with the Buyer's USD 35,000,000 proposal, subject to diligence and agreement on price mechanics. Define the equity-value bridge, cash, indebtedness, debt-like items, transaction expenses and normalized working capital, with consistent accounting policies, no double counting and an independent-expert dispute process. Require adequate financial and disclosure materials before substantive agreement. Specify closing conditions, interim operating covenants, a long-stop date and termination rights without obligating the Buyer to close before its conditions are satisfied or waived. Require specific, fair disclosures rather than blanket qualification by the data room. Negotiate meaningful representation and indemnity protection, with separate treatment for title, authority, tax and fraud, and appropriate recovery security. Preserve existing confidentiality protections and clarify that this discussion draft creates no new binding obligations.
receiver.message_back:
Thank you. The revised draft provides a useful framework, but the Buyer cannot support USD 45,000,000 on the information currently available. Our proposal remains USD 35,000,000, non-binding and subject to satisfactory diligence, required approvals and definitive documentation. Any reconsideration would require financial support for the Seller's valuation and a satisfactory overall allocation of risk.

Please provide, through an appropriately protected diligence process, historical accounts, current management accounts, forecasts and their assumptions, together with schedules of cash, debt and debt-like items, transaction expenses and normalized working capital. Please also confirm the enterprise-to-equity-value bridge underlying the Seller's price proposal.

For the next draft, please address:

• Price mechanics: agreed definitions, a working-capital target, consistent accounting policies, adjustment procedures and independent-expert resolution, without double counting.
• Closing: specified conditions, appropriate interim operating covenants, an agreed long-stop date and associated termination rights.
• Representations and disclosure: substantive protections across the listed subjects, with qualifications negotiated individually. Disclosures should fairly identify the nature and scope of exceptions; data-room availability alone should not constitute disclosure.
• Recovery: meaningful indemnification and appropriate escrow or other security, with negotiated caps, baskets and survival periods and separate treatment for fundamental matters, tax and fraud. Known material exposures should be addressed specifically.

We acknowledge the express non-binding status of the draft. Existing confidentiality obligations should remain unaffected, and any additional binding confidentiality arrangements should be expressly agreed separately. We are ready to progress diligence and definitive terms promptly, but cannot agree price or risk allocation in advance of that work.
